# Eosinophilia

**Authors:** Sruthi Kanuru, Amit Sapra

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Eosinophils are a kind of blood granulocytes that express cytoplasmic granules that contain basic proteins and bind with acidic dyes like “eosin.” They derive from bone marrow, and IL-5, IL-3, and GM-CSF stimulate their production. They have a circulating half-life of 4.5 to 8 hours. They can reside in tissues, mostly in the respiratory tract and gastrointestinal tract, for 8 to 12 days. Eosinophils are less than 5% of circulating leukocytes. Eosinophilia is defined as an increase of circulating eosinophils >500 /mm^3.  Based on the counts, eosinophilia can subdivide into different categories: mild (500 and 1500/mm^3), moderate (1500 to 5000/mm3), and severe (> 5000/mm^3). Hypereosinophilic syndrome is defined as an absolute eosinophil count greater than 1500/mm3 on two occasions at least one month apart or marked tissue eosinophilia.
